comment: FHIR is an important exchange framework, but the text may be read as making it the universal semantic and exchange solution. Aggregate reporting, imaging, laboratory, logistics and geospatial/public-health data may require other standards. FHIR versions and resources also differ in normative maturity; HL7 describes R5 as an STU while R4 combines normative and STU content: https://fhir.hl7.org/fhir/versions.html

reviewer.name: Brian O'Donnell (on behalf of HISP-UiO)
reviewer.organisation: HISP Centre at University of Oslo

Aggregate reporting, imaging, laboratory, logistics and geospatial/public-health data may require other standards. public.suggestedRevision: Describe FHIR as one (highly recommended) standards family within a governed standards portfolio. Require stated versions, national profiles/implementation guides, terminology bindings, validation and migration policy. Recognize complementary standards and non-FHIR aggregate interfaces. National standards frameworks depend on use case and maturity rather than by blanket preference.
